Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a post‑crisis programme for a future fair for all, built on active, reforming government. In the wake of the financial crash, Afghanistan and the expenses scandal, it rejects “business as usual,” pledging to secure the recovery, renew society, and restore trust in politics.

Economic strategy and fairness
- Secure the recovery by avoiding premature cuts, then more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair taxes and lower‑priority savings while protecting frontline spending on the NHS, schools, childcare and policing. Tough choices include public pay restraint, pension reform, efficiency savings and asset sales; tax fairness includes a 50p rate over £150k, a bank bonus tax, and a 1p NI rise while protecting the lowest paid.
- Reform finance to serve the real economy: tighter bank capital and pay rules, living wills, lending targets, more competition and a global levy; realise public stakes responsibly.
- Build a high‑tech, greener economy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, HS2, universal broadband, ring‑fenced science, R&D incentives, patent box, and corporate governance reform (two‑thirds takeover threshold). Create one million skilled jobs, a regional growth fund, stronger SME support and apprenticeships.

Work, welfare and living standards
- End long‑term unemployment with guarantees: jobs or training for young people after six months; mandatory job offers after two years; extend tough‑but‑fair work capability tests with support for disabled people. Minimum Wage to rise with earnings; a £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; Skills Accounts; clampdown on rogue employers.
- Help with housing and finance: stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% on £1m+ homes), more affordable homes, stronger repossession protections, a People’s Bank at the Post Office, universal access to basic bank accounts, and action on high‑cost credit.

Education and children
- Increase frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places. A legally backed 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one tuition for pupils falling behind; personal tutors in secondary; stronger leadership through accredited school groups, academies and co‑ops; parental power to trigger leadership change. Raise participation to 18, expand advanced apprenticeships and widen HE access.

NHS and care
- Protect NHS budgets, reinvest up to £20bn efficiencies, and shift to prevention and personalisation. Legal guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; mid‑life health checks; choice of qualified providers; extended GP access; talking therapies; one‑to‑one cancer nursing; more care at home.
- Create a National Care Service: free home care for the greatest needs from 2011, a cap on residential costs after two years, national standards, and expanded individual budgets. Support families with a Father’s Month, a Toddler Tax Credit, extended flexible working and an end to default retirement at 65. Re‑link the Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012 and auto‑enrol millions into pensions.

Safety, communities, immigration and culture
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood teams visible and accountable; faster action on anti‑social behaviour with a right to injunctions; expand Community Payback; use CCTV and DNA to tackle serious crime. Control immigration through the points‑based system, earned citizenship and English proficiency, aligning flows with economic need.
- Back thriving communities: protect post offices and pubs; empower supporters’ trusts in football; uphold BBC independence; deliver a golden Olympic legacy; support arts and free museums.

Green transition
- About 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 via renewables, new nuclear and clean coal/CCS; 400,000 green jobs; “pay as you save” home upgrades, smart meters, warmer homes for pensioners; move towards zero waste; protect and connect habitats, maintain the Green Belt and expand woodlands; a Supermarket Ombudsman for fair food chains.

Democratic renewal and global role
- Clean up politics and empower citizens: AV referendum, staged election of a reformed second chamber, fixed‑term parliaments, a lobbyists’ register, recall for misconduct, open data and stronger local government through Total Place.
- Support troops and veterans; a Strategic Defence Review; maintain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Lead in a reformed EU, legislate 0.7% aid from 2013, and advance climate, security and development goals.

Contrasting a pessimistic, backward‑looking Conservatism, Labour offers an optimistic, practical, progressive programme to secure recovery and build a fairer, stronger Britain.

TEXT_D:
Change that Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain (Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010)

Core purpose: hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing power — economic, social, political and financial — away from vested interests and towards citizens. After decades of red–blue, blue–red governments, the Liberal Democrats offer fundamental reform built around four priorities:

1) Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- Raise the personal allowance to £10,000, a £700 tax cut for most workers; 3.6m low earners and pensioners lifted out of income tax.
- Paid for by: taxing capital gains at income rates; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; replacing Air Passenger Duty with a fairer per‑plane duty (higher for non‑lifeline domestic flights); robust anti‑avoidance and anti‑evasion action; reform of non‑dom status.
- Credible deficit reduction: over £15bn identified savings (e.g., scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; banking levy; cap public‑sector pay rises at £400 for two years; prison reform; reduce quangos; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B). No like‑for‑like Trident replacement; Council on Financial Stability to guide the pace of cuts.

2) A fair chance for every child
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition for disadvantaged pupils; earlier SEN assessment and better teacher training.
- Free schools to innovate: an Education Freedom Act; independent Educational Standards Authority; a slimmer core curriculum; reform league tables.
- Transform 14–19 pathways: a General Diploma to combine academic and vocational learning; FE parity; right to study at college from 14.
- Scrap unfair university tuition fees, phased over six years (final‑year fees ended immediately); targeted national bursaries.

3) A fair future: jobs and green growth
- Break up the banks, separate retail from investment, reform bonuses, and create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- A UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private finance for clean energy and transport.
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 Eco Cash‑Back; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage; major youth work‑experience offer.
- Climate leadership: zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% clean electricity by 2020 (prioritising marine/offshore); home insulation up to £10,000 per home; no new coal without top‑tier CCS; reject new nuclear in favour of cheaper conservation/renewables; build a European Supergrid.
- Transport fairness: shift funding from roads to rail; cut regulated rail fares 1% below inflation annually; regulate buses locally; cancel Heathrow R3; per‑plane duty; plan for fair, revenue‑neutral road pricing later.

4) A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties
- End safe seats with fair votes (STV) and cut 150 MPs; fixed‑term parliaments; a fully elected, smaller second chamber; a written constitution via a citizens’ convention.
- Cleaner politics: recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; statutory lobbyist register; all candidates and parliamentarians tax‑resident in the UK.
- Freedom Bill: roll back the surveillance state; regulate CCTV; protect trial by jury and free speech; end blanket retention of innocent people’s DNA; scrap ID cards; stop unfair US extraditions.

Public services and communities built on fairness
- NHS: cut waste, not care; protect frontline (cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia); integrate health and social care; prevention first; patient entitlements over targets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access.
- Families: shared parental leave; flexible working for all; end child detention in immigration; stronger youth services; equal minimum wage from 16; carers’ respite.
- Older people: restore the earnings link (triple lock: earnings, prices or 2.5%); scrap compulsory retirement ages; long‑term plan for a Citizen’s Pension.
- Crime: 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; empower elected police authorities; target what works, including restorative justice; presumption against short prison sentences; evidence‑based drugs policy.
- Immigration: firm and fair — reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points system; enforce against rogue employers; earned citizenship for long‑settled families pre‑2010; humane, independent asylum system with right to work.
- Pro‑Europe, internationalist and principled abroad: lead EU climate ambition and financial reform; aid at 0.7% of GNI by 2013; defence review; fair pay/housing for forces; no like‑for‑like Trident; uphold human rights, end complicity in torture; two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade.

If you want real, lasting change that works for you, choose fairness: choose the Liberal Democrats.
